args.name: target
args.doc: A heading, tab or accordion as the page writes it, or words on it.

moves.say: {show: Heading} scrolls to a heading on the page they are on, or are taken to by a page cue, and rings it. Use the heading exactly as the site pages list or the screen lines spell it. With the label of one of the page's tabs or accordions ("Patagonia [Argentina + Chile]"), it opens it. With words that are not a heading, it rings those words: a room, an exploration, a lodge's name.
moves.doc: Scroll to a heading, open a tab or accordion, or ring words, on the page in front.

args.name: question
args.doc: The question as the page writes it.

moves.say: {faq: Question} opens that question's accordion on the page and rings it.
moves.doc: Open a question's accordion and ring it.

args.name: after_words
args.doc: Words of his still to be heard before the page may go (the holder's pacing).

moves.doc:
Open a www.explora.com page in the tab in front, once his voice has said
``after_words`` words: a full page load. The page reports ``page_changed``.
notes: A page cue is not a cue on Explora: every page is a full page load, so the brain splits his reply there and sends this itself, once the words before it are said.

moves.doc:
Load the page in front's own twin in ``language``, once his voice is quiet;
refused when it has none.

args.name: hotel_code
args.doc: The lodge's code on the booking site, such as EATA.

args.name: rooms
args.doc: Go on to the rooms and rates.

moves.doc:
On reservations.explora.com, the lodge ``hotel_code``, and with them the
arrival ``date``, ``month``, ``nights``; with ``rooms``, on to the rooms and
rates. Never past them. The page reports ``stay_state``.
notes: Dev call 2f94965e: "I'm opening the Atacama calendar for three nights", twice, and no check_availability either time: the claims.

Dev call 453f2e19: "I'll open the calendar.", "I'm selecting three nights to see the rates.", "I'm opening the rooms and rates", and no call each time; no claim matched any of them. The objects do, by the sentence's shape.

args.name: room
args.doc: The room as the rates page names it.

moves.doc:
On the rooms and rates, select ``room`` for ``travellers`` with ``bed``,
``count`` times. Never check-out itself.
notes: Objects in the singular, so a plural hears them too; "the rooms" alone is check_availability's first, and either one made keeps the sentence.

args.name: expedition_code
args.doc: The expedition's code, such as XSCM.

moves.doc: Open an expedition's enquiry form and fill in the fields given.

Press Send Message on the filled form: the visitor's own data, so only
after they ticked the reCAPTCHA and the brain checked every field.
Bring one of the visitor's Explora tabs to the front.
